posts.title: Keep the Helper, Not the Language: A Prelude for Codemode
posts.description: In the codemode posts of this series, my agent acts by writing short JavaScript programs that call its tools. Each program runs in a fresh child process, and nothing it defines reaches the next one. In the fold posts , old work leaves the model’s context as one line per finished unit. Put those two facts side by side and a long session has an obvious waste. The model writes the same small function

posts.title: When to Fold: The Model Says Done, the Cache Says When
posts.description: In the first post of this series the model folds a unit of work when it closes: the host replaces the unit’s turns with a short result and keeps the originals on disk. In the second the folded units become one title each, and the title list is merged as a binary counter so that it stays short. Both posts treated the moment of a fold as settled. The model calls fold_unit , and the fold takes effect

posts.title: Merge the Folds: A Binary Counter Over the Title List
posts.description: Last time I argued that an agent should not wait for the context window to fill. When a unit of work closes, the model says so, and the host replaces that unit’s turns with a short result and archives the originals to disk.
